proposed.explanation: Both EFID and COMI show strong FY2025 profit growth (EFID net profit up ~68% to 2.70 billion EGP; COMI net profit up ~49% to 82.26 billion EGP), and EPS improved for both. However, your stated goal is to lower risk before retirement, with low willingness and low ability to absorb losses over a 3-year horizon. The evidence provided is limited to a single year of consolidated net profit and EPS for each company. What is missing for a responsible allocation decision for a risk-averse investor includes: (1) balance-sheet data (leverage, liquidity, asset quality), (2) operating cash-flow data to confirm earnings quality, (3) dividend history and payout policy (important for a retiree seeking income), (4) multi-year trend data (only two years are shown, and one year of growth does not establish a pattern), (5) sector/industry risk context, (6) any forward guidance or known risks, and (7) volatility or drawdown history. Without these, I cannot determine whether either stock is appropriate for your risk profile, which one (if either) you should reduce, or whether the profit growth is sustainable. Your current portfolio is already concentrated in COMI (≈53% of total value), which is a concentration concern, but I cannot responsibly recommend selling without knowing the underlying risk drivers. I recommend obtaining the full annual reports (balance sheet, cash flow, notes on risk) and, if possible, a second or third year of results before making any buy/sell decision. In the meantime, your 5,000 EGP cash buffer is modest; preserving it while you gather more information is prudent.
